def factor_volatility_blended_momentum(df):
    df_copy = df.copy()
    close = df_copy['close']
    ret = close.pct_change()
    vol = ret.rolling(20).std()
    vol_ema = vol.ewm(span=20).mean()
    vol_ratio = vol / vol_ema.replace(0, np.nan)
    weight_long = np.clip(vol_ratio, 0, 1)
    roc10 = close.pct_change(10)
    roc40 = close.pct_change(40)
    factor = weight_long * roc40 + (1 - weight_long) * roc10
    df_copy['factor_volatility_blended_momentum'] = factor
    return df_copy['factor_volatility_blended_momentum']
formula: weight_long * roc40 + (1 - weight_long) * roc10, where weight_long = clip(vol/vol_ema, 0, 1), vol = rolling_std(returns, 20)
rationale: Blended momentum weighting by volatility ratio. Instead of a binary switch based on residual volatility regime, this factor continuously blends 10-day and 40-day momentum using the ratio of recent volatility (20-day rolling std of returns) to its 20-day EMA. When volatility is elevated (ratio > 1), more weight is given to the longer 40-day momentum to filter noise; when volatility is low, the faster 10-day momentum dominates. This preserves the adaptive hypothesis while eliminating the discontinuity of a hard gate, potentially improving rank stability and predictive consistency.
